title: Actionability checks and trusted input for every ref-targeted action, then rich input actions
summary: Change Quarry's ref-targeted click/type path from element.click() via Runtime.callFunctionOn to: scroll into view, wait for attached/visible/enabled/stable (poll content quads over two frames), hit-test the centre via DOM.getNodeForLocation including cross-process iframe hops, then dispatch trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent/KeyEvent. Return typed errors (covered by <tag>, not_visible, disabled) and keep element.click() only as an explicit fallback. Follow-up phase: press with modifiers, drag, select_text and paste with a per-session virtual clipboard.
whyItMatters: Every AI click passes through this executor. Untrusted synthetic clicks silently no-op on sites that ignore them or sit behind overlays; honest 'covered by cookie banner' errors let the model recover. Flaky agents are noticed immediately.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (CA056/CI115: hit-testing across nested and cross-process iframes returning hittable|covered(hitTag)|unpositioned; key synthesis bound to an input target)
others: Aside AA022 (waitForReady attached|visible|enabled|stable with 32 ms stability sampling)
Codex clipboard shim and action set for the rich-input follow-up (1 of 3, DOC-backed)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Actionability 2 of 3 sources (table-stakes); rich input 1 of 3 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded; poll getContentQuads until stable over two frames; compute the centre; DOM.getNodeForLocation per frame hop with coordinate transforms; check the hit node is the target or a descendant, else error 'covered by <tag>'; then Input.dispatchMouseEvent moved/pressed/released and dispatchKeyEvent with modifiers.

verevonToday.gap: execute_native_target_action resolves the backend node and checks isConnected, then runs element.click() inside Runtime.callFunctionOn: a synthetic, untrusted click with no visibility, stability, scroll or covered-element check (SRC, read in this audit). Only coordinate click_point uses trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent. Press carries only a key string, and a grep of contracts.rs finds no drag, paste, modifier or clipboard support.

approach: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser (chromiumoxide.rs): implement the actionability + hit-test pipeline with OOPIF coordinate transforms behind a driver capability first, add typed error codes to quarry-core contracts, then extend AgentAction (press{modifiers}, drag, select_text, paste{format}) with a per-session virtual clipboard in the page.
risks: Cross-origin iframe coordinate transforms are fiddly and regressions in existing flows are possible, so ship behind a capability flag. The rich-input phase is nice-to-have and can be deferred.

verevon.exactGap: Ref-targeted click, type and select run as in-page DOM operations through Runtime.callFunctionOn: execute_native_target_action checks only isConnected, then calls element.click() or sets the value and dispatches synthetic events (chromiumoxide.rs:1232-1330), and the non-native verified-target path does the same in a page script (chromiumoxide.rs:2026-2093). There is no scroll-into-view, visibility, enabled, stability or covered-element check and no hit-test on the ref path; only click_point (chromiumoxide.rs:2841) dispatches trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent, the legacy selector click and type use chromiumoxide's scrolling, trusted-event helpers (2828-2915), Press carries only a key string (contracts.rs:699), and the only typed target error is TargetRepairRequired (error.rs:30).
reuse: execute_native_target_action backend-node resolution and per-frame execution-context lookup (chromiumoxide.rs:1232-1290)
click_point's moved/pressed/released Input.dispatchMouseEvent sequence as the trusted dispatch primitive (chromiumoxide.rs:2841-2896)
BrowserDriverCapabilities flag pattern (lib.rs:269-286) to gate the new pipeline per driver
ActionOutcome::unknown(postcondition_required) in observation.rs, which keeps Quarry from claiming a business effect
verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser only; Quarry owns execution and must keep returning an unverified postcondition rather than claim success. The Model Plane browser.act wire schema is a closed list, so new inputs (modifiers, drag, paste) are not reachable by the model without a separate Model Plane contract change. Upload and download reuse the same native click helper and stay approval-gated, so changing the click semantics must not weaken or alter those gates.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Direction is right. Express the new failures as ErrorCode::TargetRepairRequired (409) with details.reason (covered_by, not_visible, disabled, unstable) instead of new ErrorCode variants, since ErrorCode is a wire contract shared with the Go, TypeScript and Model Plane clients. Put the pipeline behind a new BrowserDriverCapabilities flag so Browserbase, Browserless and Kernel adapters are unaffected, and leave the synthetic path for governed download clicks until trusted-click download behaviour is verified. Sequence same-frame actionability and trusted dispatch first; the cross-process iframe hit-test and the rich-input phase (modifiers, drag, select_text, paste, virtual clipboard) are separate follow-ups.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for same-frame actionability, hit-test, trusted dispatch and typed errors; the OOPIF coordinate transforms and the rich-input phase together are L and should be split out.
verevon.verdictReason: Accurately describes a real gap on every AI ref click and type; only the error-contract and capability-flag details need adjusting.

reference.corrections: Mechanism must not say Codex uses DOM.getNodeForLocation: Codex hit-tests with an in-page elementFromPoint probe (shadow-root aware) injected via DOM.resolveNode + Runtime.callFunctionOn per frame hop, using getContentQuads/getBoxModel for coordinate transforms. Order is: hit-test first, DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded only if not hittable, then poll every 25 ms (500 ms deadline, 0.5 px tolerance) for two consecutive matching samples (timer-based, not animation frames). Errors: 'covered by <tag> or otherwise not hittable', 'did not settle after scrolling', and 'couldn't be clicked' for unpositioned nodes. 'Rich input 1 of 3 (unique)' overstates: Aside also has trusted CDP input with modifiers, insertText, file-chooser interception and download events; only the virtual clipboard shim and held clicks/drag with xdotool key names are Codex-specific. Aside falls back to DOM activation (with checked-state verification) when the target is obscured rather than simply erroring.
caveats: Actionability is also built into Playwright (auto-wait), which Apify/Crawlee and Firecrawl's playwright-service inherit; the 2-of-3 count reflects custom implementations only (INF)
inputTargetToken semantics in Codex key synthesis are inferred from naming (INF); not a public CDP parameter
